title: Find an antiderivative
text: Integrate by parts with $$u=ln(x)$$ and $$dv=x^{\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} dx$$. An antiderivative is $$2\sqrt{x} \ln\left(x\right)-4\sqrt{x}$$.

title: Take the limit
text: At $$x=1$$ the antiderivative is $$-4$$. As $$x$$ approaches $$0$$ from the right, it goes to $$0$$. So the integral is $$-4$$.
